name: Avarice-Sands
geological_features: Gemstone-bearing sandstone formations exposed by wind erosion
Salt crystal caves of extraordinary size
Dust devils reaching the upper atmosphere
specific_features: Ruins of seven competing mining colonies, all failed within decades of founding
description: Avarice-Sands is a desert world whose windswept sandstone formations sparkle with embedded gemstones and precious metal deposits, a geological jackpot displayed openly on the surface as though daring passersby to try their luck. Salt crystal caves beneath the desert floor contain formations of dark crystals that fetch extraordinary prices on the technology markets, and platinum veins run through the bedrock like silver threads in orange cloth.

The breathable atmosphere carries fine particulate that glitters in the sunlight, giving the air itself a quality of gilded promise. Dust devils spin precious-stone-bearing sand into towering columns that reach the upper atmosphere, scattering wealth across the landscape in random redistribution that resets every claim.

Seven mining colonies have been established on Avarice-Sands over the past two centuries, and all seven have failed. Each followed the same pattern: initial extraction success, rapid expansion, resource conflicts between competing interests, and eventual collapse as the costs of maintaining operations in the harsh desert outstripped the value of what was extracted. Their ruins dot the landscape like cautionary monuments.

The microbial life that thrives in the salt caves may be responsible for the concentration of precious minerals, their metabolic processes acting as a biological refinery over geological time. Current prospecting ventures study the failed colonies' records with the conviction that they can succeed where others did not, a pattern so consistent it might itself be considered a natural resource of the planet: the renewable extraction of human optimism.
